findings.claim: H3 5d half-life table 7.4 vs 24.8 games + the 5d-vs-1a WIN
findings.attack: read the program's own profile CIs and DL pooling; recomputed the pairwise WIN with my own bootstrap; drop-top-5%; jackknife
findings.result: NOT A MEASUREMENT: profile CIs overlap massively ([3.94,18.46] vs [5.27,300.24]), DL tau^2=0 pools all cells to HL 8.0, settling cell non-monotone at the q->0 boundary (the JSON concedes non-resolvability). findings.severity: SUSPICIOUS (point ordering is a hypothesis, not a finding)

findings.attack: read corpus.log method: mechanical = cached-HTML re-parse; sample = live RE-FETCH (seed preregistered) but parsed with the SAME parser
findings.result: fetch-independent, parser-DEPENDENT: a systematic selector bug passes both checks. Registry/org/series-score cross-constraints bound gross errors; a consistent subtle parse bias (e.g. map-winner attribution on a layout variant) would not be caught. Not evidence of error — a limit of the verification design, stated plainly

bottom_line: The program's negative conclusions are sound and independently reproducible to the last digit. Its surviving POSITIVE leads are weaker than published: every one except H3's cold(<10) cell fails at least one of {own bucket-MDE rule, preregistered definition fidelity, drop-top-5% fragility, target-population coherence}. I would sign: 'v6 stands; nothing promotable; cold-start handling is the one lead worth new data.' I would not sign any sentence that presents 3e-EWC, event-class fade subpop positivity, the 5d half-life ordering, or compose S1 as established effects.
